title: Controller functions carry an isActive gate as well as a role check, giving Grove a system-wide pause distinct from rate limits and relayer revocation
content:
The instance-level documentation introduces a modifier absent from the general controller sections. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.4.1.3.2.1 declares `setDelegatedSigner` as `external onlyRole(RELAYER) isActive`, and adds the operator requirement: "they must ensure the contract `isActive` i.e. can process the request." The same pairing appears on `removeDelegatedSigner` (A...4.1.3.3.1), `prepareUSDeMint` (A...4.1.3.4.1), `prepareUSDeBurn` (A...4.1.3.5.1), `cooldownAssetsSUSDe` (A...4.2.3.1.1), `cooldownSharesSUSDe` (A...4.2.3.2.1) and `unstakeSUSDe` (A...4.2.3.3.1).

That gives Grove three shutdown levers at three different granularities. `isActive` is contract-wide and asset-blind — one flag stops everything. A rate limit of zero is per key, disabling one function or one venue while the rest keep running. `removeRelayer` is per actor, stopping a particular operator's access while the contract stays live for the backstop relayer.

Having all three is not redundancy, because the right response depends on where the fault is. A compromised key wants actor-level revocation; a broken integration wants key-level disabling; an unfolding systemic event wants everything stopped at once. Collapsing them into one control would force an overreaction or an underreaction in most incidents.

What the chunk does not say is who may flip `isActive` or under what conditions — the modifier appears only in function signatures, never with its own procedure. Given that it is the broadest control in the system, that is the notable omission.
description: Every Ethena instance function is declared onlyRole(RELAYER) isActive, so the contract can be made unable to process any request without touching roles or limit configuration.
